name: TrackSharp – Server Side Tracking for WooCommerce
author: TrackSharp

sections.description:
TrackSharp is a first-party server-side tracking plugin for WooCommerce that sends purchase events directly from your server to Google Analytics 4.

🎯 Rescue lost conversions – Ad blockers, ITP, and browser restrictions block up to 30% of client-side tracking. TrackSharp sends events server-to-server, ensuring your conversions are counted.

Free Features

✅ GA4 Server-Side Tracking – Send purchase events via Measurement Protocol
✅ WooCommerce Integration – Automatic order tracking with session stitching
✅ Consent-Aware – Honors WP Consent API categories (statistics, statistics-anonymous)
✅ Dashboard & Event Log – See tracked orders, revenue, and event status
✅ Setup Wizard – Simple step-by-step configuration
✅ First-Party REST API – Collect browser events via your own domain

Pro Features 🔒

Upgrade to TrackSharp Pro for advanced tracking capabilities:

🚀 Meta Conversions API – Server-side tracking for Facebook/Instagram ads with full user_data hashing
🚀 Google Ads Attribution – Capture and pass gclid, gbraid, wbraid for proper conversion attribution
🚀 Enhanced Conversions – SHA-256 hashed user data (email, phone, address) for improved GA4 matching
🚀 Priority Support – Get help directly from the developers

View Pro Plans →

How It Works

  1. A customer places an order in WooCommerce
  2. TrackSharp captures session data and ad click identifiers
  3. After payment, the purchase event is sent server-to-server to GA4
  4. Your conversion is counted even if the browser blocked client-side tracking

Consent & Privacy

  • Integrates with WP Consent API and popular CMPs
  • GA4 events require statistics consent (configurable)
  • Fallback behavior when no CMP is installed (configurable in settings)

What Gets Stored

  • Custom table: {prefix}_ws_events (event audit log)
  • Order meta: session ID, GA4 client ID, consent state
  • Cookie: ws_session_id (first-party session tracking)

Admin Pages

  • Dashboard – Overview of tracked orders and revenue
  • Events Log – Raw event log with filters and CSV export
  • Settings – GA4 credentials and consent configuration
  • Setup Wizard – Step-by-step setup with test functionality

Consent specifics

  • If WP Consent API is active, TrackSharp checks:
    • Meta: marketing must be granted.
    • GA4: statistics or statistics-anonymous (filterable).
  • If no WP Consent API is found, a fallback applies (default: “Grant immediately”). You can change this in TrackSharp → Settings.

Filters & actions (developer hooks)

Filters:
– tracksharp_ga4_requires_marketing (bool): require marketing for GA4 (default false).
– tracksharp_tracker_is_consent_granted (bool, array $payload): override final consent decision per request.
– tracksharp_tracker_frontend_consent (array): seed consent for the front-end script.
– tracksharp_session_cookie_category (string): category required to set the session cookie (default functional).
– tracksharp_consent_category_marketing / tracksharp_consent_category_statistics / tracksharp_consent_category_statistics_anonymous (strings): remap category slugs.
– tracksharp_blocked_log_events (array): event names to exclude from audit log (default view_item, viewcontent, pageview).
– tracksharp_ga4_host (string): override GA4 MP endpoint host.

Actions:
– tracksharp_prune_events (daily cron)

Privacy

TrackSharp processes event data for analytics and advertising measurement. User-provided data sent to Meta/GA4 is hashed (SHA-256) server-side when raw values are provided. Enable a CMP with WP Consent API to ensure events are sent only when the correct categories are granted. Review your legal basis and privacy policy accordingly.

Third Party Services

This plugin connects to the following external services:

Google Analytics 4 (Measurement Protocol)
TrackSharp sends purchase and conversion events server-side to Google Analytics 4 using the Measurement Protocol API. This occurs when GA4 is configured with a Measurement ID and API Secret in the plugin settings.
– Service: https://www.google-analytics.com
– Terms: https://policies.google.com/terms
– Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Meta (Facebook) Conversions API
TrackSharp sends purchase events server-side to Meta (Facebook) using the Conversions API. This occurs when Meta is configured with a Pixel ID and Access Token in the plugin settings. User data is hashed (SHA-256) before transmission as required by Meta.
– Service: https://graph.facebook.com
– Terms: https://www.facebook.com/terms.php
– Privacy Policy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy

Freemius (Licensing & Updates)
This plugin uses Freemius for plugin updates and to display optional upgrade options. If you choose to upgrade to Pro, Freemius handles license management for the Pro version and exchanges data with Freemius servers.
– Service: https://freemius.com
– Terms: https://freemius.com/terms/
– Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install via the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to TrackSharp → Setup Wizard and:
    • Enter your GA4 Measurement ID and API Secret
    • (Pro) Configure Meta Conversions API credentials
  4. (Recommended) Install WP Consent API and a CMP for consent management.
  5. Make a test order and check TrackSharp → Events to verify tracking.
sections.faq:
Does this replace my GA4/Meta browser tags?

No. TrackSharp complements your browser tags with reliable server-to-server events. You can keep your browser tags for attribution, deduping, and non-purchase events.

How are events deduplicated?

The plugin uses deterministic event_id values (e.g., purchase_{$order_id}) and sends a browser breadcrumb (audit-only) while the server event is the authoritative hit for GA4/Meta. On GA4, Measurement Protocol also carries session parameters for proper attribution.

Is it GDPR compliant?

TrackSharp integrates with WP Consent API. GA4 is allowed under statistics or statistics-anonymous (configurable), Meta under marketing. With no CMP, you can choose a fallback policy (default: grant immediately).

What cookies does it set?

  • ws_session_id — first-party session ID (functional/statistics-gated).
  • ws_atc — short-lived Add-to-Cart replay cookie (marketing-gated).
    The plugin also reads first-party copies of ad cookies (_fbp, _fbc) if present.

Which data is stored in the database?

An audit log in {$wpdb->prefix}ws_events with timestamp, channel, source, event name, HTTP status, consent, user-agent, and (if present) transaction ID and event ID.

Does it support non-WooCommerce events?

The built-in JS can post custom events to the first-party collector, but the S2S purchase stitching is tailored for WooCommerce.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • Initial release (TrackSharp UI/branding).
  • GA4 Measurement Protocol with Enhanced Conversions.
  • Meta Conversions API with hashed user_data and fbp/fbc.
  • WP Consent API integration with stats/marketing categories (+ statistics-anonymous for GA4).
  • WooCommerce order stitching and S2S purchase sending.
  • Events Log table + CSV export.
  • Setup Wizard and Test Console.
  • First-party REST collector (/wp-json/tracksharp/v1/p).
